heroHeadline: IEA: 1-in-4 New Cars Now Electric; Worst-Case Warming Ceiling Cut to 3.5°C — Solar + Wind Credit
heroSubtitle: 3,813 days since the Paris Agreement — the IEA's Global EV Outlook 2026 (May 21) confirmed 20.2 million EVs sold in 2025, with 1 in 4 new cars globally now electric and the fleet displacing 1.2 Mb/d of oil. Climate scientists (ScenarioMIP, May 19) revised the worst-case warming ceiling down from 4.5°C to 3.5°C, directly crediting rapid solar and wind deployment for making high-fossil-fuel futures implausible. BloombergNEF's New Energy Outlook 2026 found solar will become the world's largest electricity source by 2032, with global storage growing 17-fold to 3.8 TW by 2035. The Copenhagen Climate Ministerial (May 20) designated electrification — raising electricity's share of final energy to 35% by 2035 — as the core COP31 Antalya deliverable.
footerNote: Data sourced from IEA, IRENA, IPCC, UNEP, BloombergNEF, and major international outlets. All figures reflect verified, publicly available data through May 2026.
